entries.922464afde29515a: The company is headquartered in Sakai, Osaka Prefecture, and manufactures and sells nursing care products and welfare equipment, provides nursing care services, and operates e-commerce. The company and its five consolidated subsidiaries, six companies in total, make up the group. As of February 28, 2026, the number of employees was 211. The company is listed on the Standard Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Revenue for the fiscal year ended February 2026 was ¥6,394 million, and revenue from external customers by segment was ¥5,418 million for the Nursing Care Products and Welfare Equipment Manufacturing and Sales Business, ¥279 million for the Nursing Care Services Business and ¥696 million for the EC Business. A major customer is Panasonic Age-Free Co., Ltd.

entries.9f723f0d8a69788a: Its main products are welfare equipment for walking assistance, such as silver carts, walkers and canes, and it also handles daily-living support products for bathing, toileting and medication support. Silver carts and walkers are mainly manufactured at Dongguan Kowa Household Products Co., Ltd., the production base in Dongguan, China, while canes and other welfare equipment are procured from contracted factories and suppliers in Japan and overseas. Sales channels include the chain store channel for mass retailers through agents (wholesalers), the nursing care channel for nursing care service providers, and the OEM channel that responds to orders from customers, among others. Revenue from external customers was ¥5,418 million in the fiscal year ended February 2026.
entries.9fe5b5552f366162: The company mainly handles silver carts, walkers and canes designed to assist walking, as well as daily living support products for bathing, toileting and medication assistance, and develops them comprehensively under its own brand TacaoF (Teikobu). It also rents welfare equipment under the long-term care insurance system. Revenue from external customers by segment for the fiscal year ended February 2026 was ¥5,418 million for the Care Products and Welfare Equipment Manufacturing and Sales Business, ¥279 million for the Care Service Business, and ¥696 million for the EC Business.

entries.b6a73b50f8361e37: As its management philosophy, the company cites 'For tomorrow's smiles, we will give everyone love, emotion and courage,' among others, and through the development, manufacture and sale of care products and welfare equipment, it aims to improve the quality of life (QOL) of older people and contribute to a sustainable society. The medium-term management plan that started in the fiscal year ended February 2025 sets as its core policies: (1) transforming and expanding existing businesses, through stronger product differentiation and proposal capabilities by use and diversified sales channels; (2) improving operational efficiency, through unified systems, stronger links between business processes, a better workplace and optimized inventory management; and (3) redesigning brand value, through developing the new brand AURULA, launched in April 2024. It aims to evolve as a company creating living value.

entries.fd2a8b2861f1f805: A maker of walking aids that has continued to manufacture and sell silver carts since 1970. In walkers, it continuously develops products suited to users' conditions, including the lightweight, compact Teikobu Little, the forearm-support Shitorea, the Jisuta, which requires no brake operation, and the Jisuta R, which has a built-in speed-control brake. Its structure, with its own production base in Dongguan, China, combines manufacturing and sales with welfare equipment rental and EC, allowing information gathered in the field to feed into product development. This is its distinctive feature. The company is also expanding its brands, including the new AURULA brand, which emphasizes design as well as functionality.
